newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Ethnic clashes in Nigerian oil town.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic clashes in Nigerian oil town.

text.p: Youths from two rival tribes fought on Sunday in the Nigerian oil town of Warri, burning houses and cars after weeks of a fragile truce, newspapers said on Monday.
They said one person was feared dead in the clash set off by the arrest of a man alleged to have been harassing people in Warri in the midwestern state of Delta.
Order was restored several hours later when security agents intervened, they said.

Warri, where the Nigerian unit of oil giant Royal Dutch Shell Group has its western division operational headquarters, came into spotlight in March when Ijaw and Itsekiri tribesmen fought over the relocation of their local government headquarters.

The army intervened after weeks of mayhem to restore peace and a judicial commission is sitting to establish the cause of the crisis, which took scores of lives and forced Shell to close several oil wells.
A Shell spokesman in Lagos said the company's operations had not been affected by the latest clashes. "Everything is running okay," he said.
